automated_validation.linux_metrics_test_scope: core, host mTLS/parser, daemon cache and snapshot visibility

deployment.coordination: Previous host user explicitly released the machine before live telemetry testing
deployment.method: Controller-only compatibility bundle through the installed guarded updater
deployment.compatibility: Only daemon and CLI binaries changed; installed Python host and guest adapters, native helpers, firewall, and deployment boundary were preserved byte-for-byte

authenticated_snapshots.transport: Disposable enrolled Linux CLI device over the normal QUIC/TLS control protocol

guest_root_filesystem_proof.method: Compare authenticated controller samples with guest os.statvfs('/') before, during, and after a temporary posix_fallocate allocation
guest_root_filesystem_proof.result: Actual guest filesystem allocation rose by the temporary allocation and recovered within 68 KiB of the original controller sample

independent_review_corrections.re_review: No blocking findings; additional malformed-tail injection regression and missing-identity diagnostic corrected afterward
independent_review_corrections.final_local_validation: 309 non-GUI Rust tests, 126 native desktop tests, 136 Python host tests, workspace Clippy, formatting, and signed app packaging passed after the reviewed parent PR fixes
independent_review_corrections.reason: resolvr-box was released to another testing thread and remains reserved; the recorded live proof precedes these source corrections

parent_pr_review_followup.focused_re_review: No blockers; its non-blocking findings were corrected with regressions before publishing

limitations: Shared Incus exposition does not provide cryptographic per-VM provenance; on versions with unescaped labels, a malicious replacement guest agent could forge complete metric lines. Telemetry is never an admission, authorization, or billing input
Annual metrics client certificate renewal is documented and checked during setup; an advance-expiry GUI warning is not implemented
The rebuilt Mac CLI required normal macOS Keychain approval; its blocked test process was stopped without changing Keychain permissions or adding plaintext credentials
Live authenticated snapshots were verified with the temporary Linux client, not by bypassing Mac Keychain
The native GUI passed deterministic screenshot and interaction tests, and the signed app was rebuilt; visual acceptance of live data in the reopened Mac app remains an operator step
Live outage injection was not performed on the shared host; automated tests cover stale data, collection failure, recovery, counter resets, and member visibility
